reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that elastic undulations with 1–2 nm wavelength can form in CoCrFeMnNi at ~4 GPa and act as twin precursors, but it does not address interfacial roughness as a source of such undulations, nor the proposed shift in deformation mechanism under creep conditions at 0.6× yield stress. The link between roughness and undulation-induced twin nucleation is a key premise without direct support.
premises: Elastic field undulations with 1–2 nm wavelength can form in CoCrFeMnNi HEA at ~4 GPa shear stress
These undulations serve as a mechanistic precursor for twin nucleation
Nanoscale interfacial roughness can generate elastic field undulations that act as stress concentrators
Twin nucleation and growth can progressively shift deformation from dislocation-mediated to twin-assisted plasticity
This mechanism operates under sustained loading at ~0.6× yield stress and moderate temperatures
